definitions.explanation: A feeling of friendliness or kindness toward someone. Refers to benevolent feelings or considerate actions done out of genuine care.
Romantic feelings or attraction toward someone. A somewhat indirect and understated way to describe having feelings for someone.

examples.japanese: ご{好意|こうい}に{感謝|かんしゃ}します。
{彼|かれ}の{好意|こうい}を{無駄|むだ}にしたくない。
examples.english: I don't want to waste his kindness.

examples.japanese: {好意|こうい}で{言|い}っているのだから、{素直|すなお}に{受|う}け{取|と}った{方|ほう}がいい。
examples.english: They're saying it out of goodwill, so you should accept it graciously.

examples.japanese: {彼女|かのじょ}に{好意|こうい}を{持|も}っている。
{相手|あいて}が{好意|こうい}を{寄|よ}せていることに{気|き}づいた。
examples.english: I realized that the other person had feelings for me.

examples.japanese: {彼|かれ}の{態度|たいど}から{好意|こうい}があることは{明|あき}らかだった。
examples.english: It was obvious from his attitude that he had romantic feelings.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {好意|こうい}を{持|も}つ: to have goodwill toward / to have romantic feelings for
- {好意|こうい}を{寄|よ}せる: to show affection, to have feelings for (romantic)
- {好意|こうい}に{甘|あま}える: to take advantage of someone's kindness
- {好意|こうい}で: out of goodwill
- ご{好意|こうい}: your kindness (polite)

SIMILAR WORDS:
{好意|こうい} vs {親切|しんせつ}: Both express kindness, but {好意|こうい} emphasizes the feeling behind the action, while {親切|しんせつ} emphasizes the kind act itself. {好意|こうい} can also imply romantic interest, which {親切|しんせつ} cannot.

{好意|こうい} vs {厚意|こうい}: Both are read こうい and mean goodwill/kindness. {厚意|こうい} is more formal and emphasizes deep, heartfelt kindness. {好意|こうい} is more general and can include romantic overtones.
